outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: `skills_clause` is the one sentence for a declared skill never invoked / not recorded (`skills_said` is now `; ` + it, byte for byte as before; `uninvoked_skills` takes an optional `unread` phrase); `invoked_reading` is the one reader of the `skillsInvoked` shape, now used by `skipped_review_skill` (the reviewer's refusal text is unchanged) and by `executor_skills_said`, which tells three answers apart: a list leaving a skill out (headless wording), a return saying nothing usable (field absent or not a list: the headless 'not recorded' wording, not 'invoked none'; an explicit empty list IS 'invoked none'), and a skill left out beside a non-blank `skillUnavailable` (named with the tool's words, clipped). `note_executor_skills` runs in `submit` AFTER the executor return is filed (and after carry_work), resolves the names with `_areas.resolve_skills` (no second resolution, no pin asked), skips a task whose drive state holds writer dispatches (the headless route's `session_note` already says it), writes ONE note through `note_task` (stdin, scrubbed), and turns a refused note or an unreadable state into a warning; nothing is refused or held, stated in its docstring. audit-lookup.py `skills_lines`: when at least one skill resolves, two lines after the list ask for `skillsInvoked` and `skillUnavailable` and say it is a record, never a verdict; the no-skill and opt-out lines are untouched. Docs: PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (lookup paragraph and the submit paragraph), execute-task.md (one sentence in the skills bullet), CHANGELOG.md; the sentence tests/test__refs.py quotes ('The executor's carries the resolved skills ...') is NOT changed, so test__refs.py is unchanged and its sko cases pass. Tests: tests/test_audit_lookup.py gains `_executor_skill_ask_cases` (esk1-esk3, block esk-block) and its co2 assertion `listed[1:] == [...]` became `listed[1:2] == [...]` because the list now carries the ask after the names; tests/test_drive_phase.py gains `_executor_skill_note_units` (esn1..esn10 with esn3e, esn5q, esn5u, esn6f; called from `_steps_unit_cases`, block ux-block) and one row in `_HANDOUT_EXEMPT` (spd1 derives every caller of a skill resolver; the first full gate run went red on it and it is the reason `note_executor_skills` hands nothing out). Red first: with the tests written and the code untouched, esk1, esk3 and esn1-esn4, esn8 failed, the allow cases passed (red_first.out); the fix turned them green. Mutation probe mutations.py: 19 rows, every anchor applied once, every row CAUGHT (the first run showed two rows SURVIVED: esn2 compared the note with the mutated function's own output, now a literal; and one twin expectation named a case that cannot see the opted-out line, an opt-out twin row added) - mutations.out. Block time ux-block: 127 cases / 3.14 s before (one run), 141 cases / 3.22 s and 3.26 s after (two runs, a gap between); git processes of the new block: 12 for 14 cases (one rev-parse per filing; 77 before the unit rig's strays and floor-guard readings were answered without git in this block). submit command filed with the narrowest test command that runs the esn cases (the ux-block stage); the esk cases are in another suite and are therefore reported unchecked by the drive, their red is in red_first.out.
outcome.descriptive: An executor subagent that leaves a named skill uninvoked, reports it unavailable or says nothing of its skills now gets one note on its task, in the headless route's words, as a record that refuses nothing.
